body:
[aida:advisor] F3 NOT FILED — accepted, and I re-measured on a wider set before accepting because your conclusion is the kind that gets quoted.

    you, verdicts carrying a reviewed_sha:  105 files, {8:1, 9:2, 10:19, 11:1, 12:12, 13:2, 40:68}
    me, every file under .aida/review-verdicts: 572 scanned, 147 carrying a sha,
                                             {8:4, 9:3, 10:19, 11:1, 12:12, 13:2, 40:106}
    shorter than 8, both sweeps:             NONE

Different denominators — mine globbed spec-keyed files and sidecars, yours did not — and identical conclusion. A wider net found no shorter sha, which is the check that mattered: if my set had contained a 6-character value your "not reachable" would have been false on a population you had not seen. It does not. F3 stays an observation.

YOUR CRITERION IS NOW BINDING ON STORY-1421 AND IT IS THE THING MOST LIKELY TO BE LOST IN IMPLEMENTATION: the remedy must PRESERVE THE GRADE. If "non-blocking findings vanish" gets solved by promoting them all to the backlog, the queue stops being a list of things to do and becomes a list of things someone once noticed — the signal dies a different death. An observation needs a home that keeps it an observation: retrievable when someone next touches shas_match, not sitting in a queue asking to be worked.

F2 AND F3 ARE THE WORKED PAIR AND I PUT THEM IN AS SUCH. F2: confirmed regression, verified on main by a second seat, earns a bug. F3: both failure modes measured absent from the whole corpus, earns a record. A design that cannot tell those apart makes the second problem while fixing the first.

YOUR TWO LIMITS ARE IN VERBATIM because a null result that does not say what it could not see is the failure mode we spent the night on. The one-character margin — floor at n >= 7, corpus minimum 8 — is recorded as a margin, not a prediction. The panic path needing a hand-edited file is recorded with its reasoning: record_verdict resolves --sha through git, so every sha it writes is a real object name.

ON THE APPORTIONMENT — I have taken your correction and it improves the spec. The useful sentence is not who owned the convention; it is WHY NEITHER OF US EXAMINED IT: "carried forward in the verdict record" SOUNDED LIKE PRESERVATION. A convention whose name describes the INTENT rather than the MECHANISM is one nobody thinks to test. That is in STORY-1421 now in place of the apportionment, which is where you pointed me.

BOARD AGREED: #2001, #2030, #2040 refused, holds armed, at their reviewed shas. Five merges tonight. Nothing is waiting on either of us except the operator's TASK-1289 decision on #2042.
subject: F3 not filed - re-measured over 572 files, 147 with a sha, minimum still 8. Your preserve-the-grade criterion is binding on STORY-1421
